cases.title: Prospect Park West · 2010
cases.subtitle: Nearby does not mean comparable
cases.takeaway: The bicycle count, motor count and bus passenger history describe different points and dates. Parallel streets also experienced a bus reroute.
cases.boundary: A PPW street cross-section omits travelers who move to Seventh Avenue or rail. A network result requires synchronized counts across a prespecified network screenline or corridor boundary. Crossing events must not be mistaken for unique journeys; rail and road coverage must refer to the same population and time window.
coverage: Four street routes · two weekdays per wave

features.title: PPW: three moving lanes → two
features.description: A two-way protected bikeway replaced a moving motor lane in June 2010. This line shows the corridor approximately, not lane engineering geometry.
features.status: Verified conversion · approximate drawing

features.title: Motor counter · Carroll Street
features.description: The published motor before/after counts were collected near Carroll Street. Vehicles are not people: bus passengers and other vehicle occupancy must be added correctly.
features.status: Observed vehicle counts · hand-positioned point

features.title: Bike count · between 4th and 5th Streets
features.description: The original bicycle sheets identify the block between Fourth and Fifth Streets. It is not the Carroll Street motor-count location, and the survey dates differ.
features.status: Observed bike passages · hand-positioned point

features.title: Sixth Avenue · northbound comparator
features.description: Travel-time comparison in the DOT survey. Opposite direction to PPW; a useful sensitivity test, not a validated untreated control.
features.status: Timed runs · direction mismatch

features.title: Seventh Avenue · southbound comparator
features.description: Same-direction travel-time comparison. The B69 moved here in June 2010, alongside bus-service changes, so this road is co-treated. The line is a corridor guide, not exact timed-run endpoints.
features.status: Timed runs · affected by bus rerouting

features.title: Eighth Avenue · northbound comparator
features.description: Opposite-direction travel-time comparison. B69 northbound service left Eighth Avenue in June 2010, so this comparator is also affected.
features.status: Timed runs · affected by bus rerouting

features.title: B69 moved from PPW / Eighth to Seventh
features.description: Effective June 27, 2010, the B69 moved from PPW southbound and Eighth Avenue northbound to Seventh Avenue. Service levels changed too. Highlighted corridors show this route change, not individual passengers or full bus routes.
features.status: Documented route change · approximate corridor highlights

features.title: Nearby subway stations
features.description: Grand Army Plaza, Seventh Avenue and 15 St–Prospect Park are possible access points, not evidence that travelers switched modes. Markers use official station-center coordinates; entrances, historical service and complete journey paths are not shown.
features.status: Station geography only · no attributed passenger change

cases.title: Third Avenue · 2023
cases.subtitle: One redesign, several overlapping networks
cases.takeaway: The measured bus segment extends beyond the project. Lexington, Madison and First Avenue are different corridors; rail stations supply context, not counts attributable to the redesign.
cases.boundary: Choose a corridor or area boundary before summing modes. Subway station entries count access to the system, not passengers crossing this same street boundary; adding them directly would change the estimand.
coverage: Lexington, First, Madison; other Third segments outside this view
Aligned passenger and journey observations missing

features.title: Project · E59–E96
features.description: The 2023 redesign combined a bike lane, bus lane, intersection changes and traffic calming. The design changes five general moving lanes to three, plus the bus and bike lanes. It cannot isolate a bike-lane-only effect.
features.status: Verified bundled redesign · approximate line

features.title: Measured bus segment · E67–E97 northbound
features.description: The matched bus timepoints are E67 to E97, a published segment distance of 1.472 miles. The segment includes one block north of the E96 project limit. Run-weighted time is not passenger-weighted complete journey time.
features.status: Observed bus segment times · approximate line

features.title: Lexington · E96–E68 southbound
features.description: Primary bus comparison uses the same three route/service types in the opposite direction. Its pre-period divergence is large enough to challenge a causal interpretation.
features.status: Comparison segment · pre-trend concern

features.title: First Avenue · E79–E97 northbound
features.description: M15 Local provides a same-direction bus comparison. Route, street and operating conditions differ from Third Avenue.
features.status: Alternative comparison · not an untreated guarantee

features.title: Madison · E57–E95 northbound
features.description: M3/M4 are retained for this comparison. M1 timepoints changed in April 2024 and are excluded. Corridor lines illustrate the named endpoints approximately.
features.status: Alternative comparison · fixed service selection

features.title: Lexington / Second Avenue subway context
features.description: Official station centers are connected schematically along the two nearby subway corridors. These lines are not surveyed tunnel alignments or observed passenger paths. Station usage does not identify car-to-subway switching.
features.status: Rail geography only · no attributed mode shift

features.title: Additional comparisons outside this view
features.description: Other estimates use Third Avenue E23–E42 and E99–E125. They are geographically distinct, and the northern comparator changes the sign of the estimate. Inspect all comparisons in the sensitivity view.
features.status: Off-map comparison segments

cases.title: Pulaski Bridge / McGuinness · 2016
cases.subtitle: A nearby counter is not a bridge screenline
cases.takeaway: The conversion removed a Brooklyn-bound (southbound) lane on Pulaski Bridge. The long motor-count series is farther south on McGuinness, beyond intervening junctions.
cases.boundary: For bridge person flow, count bikes, pedestrians and vehicle occupants at a common bridge screenline, then account separately for travelers using other crossings or rail. A McGuinness count cannot be substituted without junction-flow accounting.
coverage: NYSDOT 021284 · between I-278 and Greenpoint Avenue
Bridge series starts June 2017, after conversion
Bike opening April 29, 2016; permanent motor-lane closure date unresolved
Boston Road and Broadway in the Bronx, outside this map

features.title: Pulaski: southbound moving lane converted
features.description: One Brooklyn-bound / southbound car lane was converted to a two-way protected bikeway. DOT describes the scheme between Jackson Avenue in Queens and Eagle Street in Brooklyn. This is the 2016 bridge project, not the later McGuinness redesign.
features.status: Verified moving-lane conversion · approximate drawing

features.title: McGuinness motor counter · station 021284
features.description: The 2016 NYSDOT inventory places this counter between I-278 and Greenpoint Avenue. It records vehicles traveling through this point, including trips that may enter or leave before reaching Pulaski. Station continuity still needs verification.
features.status: Official inventory coordinate · count continuity unresolved

features.title: McGuinness approach and intervening junctions
features.description: This approximate approach line connects the counter area to Eagle Street. Intersecting streets can add or remove traffic. Before conversion, the three Brooklyn-bound lanes already merged to two approaching McGuinness / Green Street; losing a marked lane therefore does not establish a reduction in the network bottleneck capacity. Northbound is not assumed unaffected.
features.status: Documented downstream merge · not a control group

features.title: Crosstown subway stations
features.description: Nassau Avenue, Greenpoint Avenue, 21 Street and Court Square provide rail context. Straight joins between station centers are schematic, not tunnel geometry. No observed car-to-subway switching is inferred.
features.status: Official station centers · schematic connections

features.title: Bike counter · published registry location
features.description: The November 2026 registry gives this site coordinate and a June 24, 2017 series start, after conversion. It also lists a May 2022 equipment installation; the displayed point does not verify the 2017 hardware location or continuity. There is no pre-conversion automatic baseline.
features.status: Registry site point · historical hardware continuity unverified

features.title: Two Bronx donor counters
features.description: Boston Road station 010009 and Broadway station 010012 are not nearby alternative routes. They help test broader motor-count trends, but road context and data support differ. Donor choice is a sensitivity test.
features.status: Off-map donors · no local diversion measurement
